answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with one-bond-per-chip. Each agent presents a signed kernel attestation bearing a copper fuse serial burned into its silicon, and posts a bond that is slashed if any second identity claims that serial. Ledger replay cancels duplicates within that serial's island, so a copied quote cannot spend twice. A thousand Sybils thus cost a thousand fused chips plus a thousand forfeited bonds; cloning one kernel across islands grants no extra capped budget and only destroys the stake.
